newsitem.title: USA: World Bank approves loans for Peru debt deal.
newsitem.headline: World Bank approves loans for Peru debt deal.

text.p: The World Bank said Tuesday it had approved two loans to support Peru's Brady-style agreement with private creditors to restructure $7.98 billion of its commercial debt.
The World Bank said in a press release it had approved a $183 million loan for debt and debt service reduction and a $100 million loan for pension system reform in Peru.
Half of the latter loan will be earmarked to support the debt reduction deal, which will offer Peru's creditors a menu of Brady bonds and a debt buy-back option, the World Bank added.

The World Bank added that, under the pension system reform program, Peru would use the proceeds from past privatizations to deposit $1.0 billion in a trust fund to secure long-term pension obligations.

"The decision to use privatization proceeds to back pensions obligations is an excellent measure of self-discipline which confirms the government's commitment to stay the course," World Bank economist Eduardo Favaro said.
The Peruvian government had announced last month that March 7 would be the closing date for its Brady deal, which has been several years in the making.

Peru was also seeking a similar loan from the Inter-American Development Bank, which together with the World Bank loan and some $635 million from its own reserves would go to cover the up-front costs of the Brady plan.
